website.description: Dalamud plugin: call anything in any loaded plugin, directly. Reflection bridge + flow engine + SND-compatible triggers.
website.readmeExcerpt:
# Conduit

**Alpha.** Built for and used on a private multi-client setup; the expression syntax, flow language and
commands can still change between releases. Everything here bypasses other plugins' guards by design — read
"Things worth knowing" before pointing it at anything.

A Dalamud plugin that calls into **any other loaded plugin's internals** — private statics, gated
methods, everything — plus a task engine for sequencing those calls across plugins.

## Why

A plugin's IPC surface is whatever its author chose to publish, and any wrapper around it inherits
whatever the author gated it behind. Two concrete walls this removes:

- **`IPC.AutoRetainer.Relog` silently returns false whenever you are logged in.** The IPC method wraps
  its call to `MultiMode.Relog` in `if (Utils.CanAutoLogin())`, and `CanAutoLogin()` requires
  `!IsLoggedIn`. Every in-plugin call site — `/ays relog`, the config GUI buttons — calls
  `MultiMode.Relog` directly with no such gate and works fine. Conduit reaches the same method.
- **SND's `IPC` Lua module is a hardcoded list** of 20 plugins compiled into SND
  (`SomethingNeedDoing/External/*.cs`). Anything not on that list — XA-Slave, ChilledLeves,
  Mass-Withdraw, Henchman — is unreachable from Lua no matter what IPC it publishes.

The general effect: no more forking a plugin just to add one entry point.

## Expression syntax

```
<Plugin>::<Type>.<Member>.<Method>(args)[index]
```

- The plugin is matched on internal name, then display name, then unique prefix.
- The root is the longest leading run of names that resolves to a type in the plugin's **load
  context** (its own assembly plus anything bundled beside it, ECommons included). `MultiMode.Relog`
  and `AutoRetainer.Scheduler.Handlers.MultiMode.Relog` reach the same place.
- `$` is the plugin's own instance: `XASlave::$`.
- Anything not resolving to a type starts from the plugin instance, and statics resolve off that
  instance's type — so `AutoRetainer::C.OfflineData` reaches the `internal static Config C` on
  AutoRetainer's plugin class without naming the class.
- Arguments are literals (`1`, `-2`, `3.5`, `0x1F`, `true`, `null`, `"quoted"`, `bare`) or `@variable`
  references inside a flow. A bare word is a string, so enum members can be written unquoted.
- Private, internal and inherited members all resolve. Overloads are ranked by how faithfully each
  argument converts, so a number binds to an enum parameter and `null` is expressible — neither of
  which the usual `GetMethod(name, argTypes)` approach can express.

## Commands

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `/co <expression>` | evaluate |
| `/co dump <expression>` | expand the result's members |
| `/co last` | repeat the last result |
| `/co plugins [filter]` | list loaded plugins |
| `/co types <plugin> [filter]` | list a plugin's types |
| `/co members <plugin>::<Type> [filter]` | list a type's members, with signatures |
| `/co flow list \| run <name> \| stop \| status \| reload` | drive flows |
| `/co trigger add <event> <flow> [filter] \| list \| remove <index>` | bind flows to SND-compatible events |
| `/co ipc [filter]` | list live IPC gates in the process |
| `/co station [status \| here \| on \| off]` | park the character at a spot via vnavmesh |
| `/co bridge` | status of the file bridge (see below) |
| `/co clip on\|off`, `/co echo on\|off` | result mirroring |
| `/co` | open the window |

`/conduit` is the same command; `/co` is the alias. If another plugin already owns `/co`, that is
logged at load and `/conduit` still works.

The **Browser** tab lists what a loaded plugin actually exposes right now. For closed-source targets
this replaces decompiling them just to learn a method name.

## Calling it from SND Lua

SND cannot call Conduit's IPC — its IPC module is compiled against a fixed plugin list. So Lua drives
the chat command and reads results back through the clipboard, which SND *can* reach
(`System.GetClipboardText()`, `SystemModule.cs`):

```lua
yield('/co AutoRetainer::C.OfflineData')
yield('/wait 0.2')
local result = json.decode(System.GetClipboardText())   -- { ok, error, type, value, outs }
if not result.ok then yield('/echo ' .. result.error) end
```

**The `/wait` matters.** The Win32 clipboard is a single global lock and any process holding it makes
the write fail — measured at roughly two failures in three single-attempt writes on a machine running
dozens of clients. Conduit therefore retries once per frame for up to 20 frames, so the write is not
necessarily done when the command returns. Observed successes at attempt 4 and attempt 7. `/wait 0.2`
covers the full budget several times over; reading immediately can get stale content.

Clipboard mirroring is **off** by default (`/co clip on` turns it on, per client — the clipboard is one global
slot per machine). Conditions polled every frame
inside a flow are deliberately *not* mirrored, or they would rewrite the clipboard at framerate.

## Flows

One step per line. Run with `/co flow run <name> [var=value ...]`, from a macro or the Flows tab.

Flows come from two places:

- **The library** — `.flow` files under [Conduit/Flows/](Conduit/Flows/), copied next to the DLL at
  build time. A rebuild deploys them and the dev-linked client picks them up on its automatic reload.
  Read-only, version-controlled, and never touches `pluginConfigs` — which matters because a running
  client rewrites its own config from memory, silently reverting hand-edits.
- **Config flows** — authored in the Flows tab, per client. A config flow overrides a library flow of
  the same name, so a shipped flow can be adjusted on one client without editing the file.

`/co flow list` shows both, marking library entries. `/co flow reload` re-reads the library without a
restart.

Seed variables are what make a library flow reusable — one file serves every character:

```
/co flow run ar-relog index=1
```

Inside the flow, `@index` can be used anywhere a literal can, including as a collection index
(`AutoRetainer::C.OfflineData[@index]`).

```
call      AutoRetainer::MultiMode.Relog("Alt Name") -> ok
waituntil ChilledLeves::$.Ready timeout 15000
wait      2s
abortif   XASlave::$.HasError
chat      /echo relogged, result was @ok
echo      relogged, result was @ok
set       target 12
```

| Step | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `call <expr> [-> var]` | evaluate once, optionally capture; a failure aborts the flow |
| `waituntil <expr> [timeout <ms>]` | re-evaluate each frame until truthy; an unevaluatable condition counts as not-yet-true and the timeout ends it |
| `wait <ms\|s>` | frame-polled, never blocks |
| `abortif <expr>` | stop the flow if truthy |
| `chat <command>` | execute a slash command as if typed in chat, `@vars` substituted |
| `echo <text>` | print to chat, `@vars` substituted |
| `set <var> <value>` | assign a literal |
| `repeat <count> [-> var]` … `end` | run the block N times; N is a literal or an expression evaluated once on entry (0 skips the block, which is the language's `if`); the optional variable receives the 0-based index |

Steps run on the framework thread through an ECommons `TaskManager`, one step per queued task.

A flow aborts on the first failed step — there is no `try`/`finally`, so never leave a state restore only
at the end of a flow. `waituntil` and `abortif` fail in opposite directions: an unevaluatable `waituntil`
counts as not-yet-true and dies on its timeout; an unevaluatable `abortif` aborts, because a guard that
cannot evaluate is a broken guard.

## Triggers

Flows can be bound to the event set SomethingNeedDoing 15.8 exposes — `OnLogin`, `OnLogout`,
`OnTerritoryChange`, `OnUpdate`, `OnConditionChange`, `OnCombatStart`/`End`, `OnChatMessage`, `OnAddonEvent`,
`OnActivePluginsChanged`, `OnDutyStarted`/`Wiped`/`Completed`, `OnEmote` — from the Triggers tab or
`/co trigger add <event> <flow> [filter]`. Filters: `OnAddonEvent <addon> [event]`,
`OnConditionChange <condition> [value]`, `OnChatMessage <substring>`. Different flows run concurrently; a
second start of a flow already running is dropped. `OnAutoRetainerCharacterPostProcess` is not a binding but
`Config.PostProcessFlow`: Conduit registers as an AutoRetainer post-process consumer and runs that flow per
character while AutoRetainer holds it, releasing the lease on completion, failure, abort, a 4-minute cap, and
unload. It ships empty (inert).

## The file bridge

For driving a client from outside the game: write `ConduitCommand.json`
(`{"id":..,"expressions":[..]}` or `{"id":..,"flow":"name","vars":{..}}`) into the plugin's config
directory and read `ConduitResponse.json` back. Commands are claimed atomically (each executes at most once),
responses are published atomically, and a request written before the current plugin instance started is
refused rather than replayed. Match on your own `id`; an ack is not a success — verify the effect. Budget:
256 KB per command file, 256 expressions, 8 KB per expression. `/co bridge` shows the state and paths.
[BUSY-LOCK.md](BUSY-LOCK.md) describes the busy lock and activity file written beside it.

## Things worth knowing

- **Everything runs on the framework thread.** Almost anything reachable through the bridge ends up
  touching game memory, and calling that from a pool thread corrupts state rather than throwing.
- **Bypassing a target's IPC bypasses whatever that IPC checked first** — availability, occupancy,
  login state. Those checks are now the caller's to make. That is the point, and it is also the
  failure mode.
- **Driving another plugin's UI still obeys the reentrancy rules.** Back-to-back synthetic
  `FireCallback`s with no frame boundary between them crash native code; pad them with a `wait` step.
- **Handles are invalidated three ways** — the load context's `Unloading` event, ECommons' installed-
  plugins-changed event, and a 5-second lifetime — because a dev rebuild usually keeps the same
  version number, which makes a reload invisible to the version-comparison check alone. On expiry the
  handle is reused if the instance is unchanged, so the type index is not rebuilt while a flow polls.

## Building

```
dotnet build -c Release Conduit/Conduit.csproj
```

Requires the .NET 10 SDK and Dalamud's dev libraries (`%appdata%/XIVLauncher/addon/Hooks/dev/`).

ECommons is a git submodule at `ECommons/` — clone with `--recurse-submodules` (or
`git submodule update --init`). The build takes it from there when present, else from a shared clone beside
the sibling forks; `-p:ECommonsPath=<path to ECommons.csproj>` overrides both, and the build fails with that
message if none is found.

## Installing

Add `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/barnicskolaci/Conduit/main/repo.json` as a custom plugin repository in
Dalamud's settings, or download `latest.zip` from a release and load it as a dev plugin.

## Tests

```
dotnet run -c Release --project Conduit.Tests
```

Compiles the pure-logic files directly — the expression parser, the coercion/overload rules, and the
flow parser — and asserts against them without needing the game.

`python tools/anonymity-check.py` greps the tree for private-setup identifiers (client names, characters,
host paths) and fails if any are present; CI runs both.
